reviews.title: Not much personalization
reviews.text:
The app is cute and I enjoy collecting the Pokemon. It just feels odd to me that it literally talks about how the best amount of sleep is what makes you feel best, but you’re locked in to an arbitrary 8 hours and 20 minutes goal to get the max amount of sleep points. You also can’t change the meal times at all, so if you’re on a third shift schedule it’s a struggle to remember to feed your Snorlax. It’s fine if you’re just using it as a sleep tracker but if you’re more interested in the game aspect of it then it can get frustrating. It would also be nice to be able to skip or turn off the Snorlax level up cutscene things. Especially when it triggers multiple times in a row while you’re in a hurry

That said, they have been updating the game regularly and have already added in a bunch of QOL stuff as well as new content. So I expect that things will only get better as time goes on

reviews.title: Actually a decent sleep tracker but…
reviews.text:
It’s honestly a great concept. What better way to track how well you sleeping than to add some Pokémon flare to it? Complete your Pokédex by befriending Pokémon who come and sleep by your side. Raise your Snorlax by making you sure you build the best team possible and it will reward you.

All-in-all, it’s a great game with a great community. I just wish the developers would allow us to play other things in the background. Or at minimum, add white noise as an option for the songs. As cute as the music is, it’s kinda hard to fall asleep to. And I don’t like that it stops playing after about 20ish mins?

There’s definitely room for improvement. Please consider incorporating our feedback.

Sincerely,
A light sleeper

reviews.title: ⭐ 1 Star — Pokémon Sleep Could Be So Much Better
reviews.text:
I really wanted to enjoy Pokémon Sleep, especially as a longtime Pokémon GO player, but right now I find the game boring and unnecessarily complicated. Too much of the gameplay revolves around managing Snorlax, collecting ingredients, and worrying about breakfast, lunch, and dinner. It feels more like a chore than something that makes me excited to go to sleep.

I think Pokémon Sleep could be amazing if it had much deeper integration with Pokémon GO.

Imagine going to sleep and having your sleep determine what Pokémon you encounter. The better and more consistent your sleep, the better your chances of discovering rarer Pokémon. When you wake up, the game could give you three Pokémon to choose from, and you could pick one to keep or transfer to Pokémon GO.

After completing seven nights of healthy sleep goals, you could even unlock a chance of encountering a Legendary Pokémon.

I would also love the ability to use my Pokémon GO Buddy in Pokémon Sleep instead of always building the experience around Snorlax. You could adventure with your Buddy during the day in Pokémon GO and then have that same Pokémon sleep alongside you at night.

There could even be special rewards, Buddy Hearts, Candy, ribbons, or other bonuses that carry between the two games.

Pokémon Sleep already supports devices such as Pokémon GO Plus + and smartwatches. Take advantage of that connection and make Pokémon GO and Pokémon Sleep feel like one continuous adventure:

Play Pokémon GO during the day. Sleep and discover Pokémon at night. Wake up, choose your Pokémon, and continue your adventure in Pokémon GO.

I love the idea behind Pokémon Sleep. I just don’t enjoy the current gameplay loop. Give Pokémon GO players a meaningful connection between the two games and I would gladly come back and change this to five stars.

reviews.title: Dear Niantic…You broke the Sleep Feature
reviews.text:
I love my Pokémon Plus + ball for tracking sleep. And up until tracking feature changed from the ball to my phone, I was using it every night to track my sleep and feed my Snorlax. 

Why did moving it to the phone break the feature?! Because now I can no longer listen to my Audible books to go to sleep while at the same time putting Pokémon Sleep into sleep tracking mode. Since the tracker is on the phone, when I enable tracking it stops the Audible playback that was playing in the background (with a sleep timer). When it was on the ball, I could push the button, Pikachu would sing his lullaby and start tracking. All while being completely separate from Audible playback on my phone. 

I’ve used other sleep trackers on my phone in the past that allowed Audible or Spotify to play in the background. So, it’s possible. 

Please fix this feature so that I can listen to my Audible books to go to sleep, like I have every night for over a decade, AND use Pokémon Sleep to track my sleep, preferably back on the physical Plus + ball, but if not, then fixed on the phone app.

reviews.title: The cutest sleep tracker- NEEDS a dark mode
reviews.text:
I’ve tracked my sleep with a variety of different apps, and this is the only one I’ve stuck with- it’s been about a year of consistent logging. Adorable, broadly self-paced, and low-stakes with no ads! It feels like a little treat to see what Pokemon show up for research and the shiny rate is way higher than any of the mainline Pokemon games. Runs nicely on iPhone 15 pro, the animations and Pokemon cries are perfect. Love the new Nap Island feature for making it easier to level helpers, too.

Game NEEDS a dark mode or something. It would be cute if they changed throughout the day to match the game’s day/night cycle, but I would be totally satisfied with a toggle switch in the settings (Light/Dark/Match system).

Minor issues- Some of the “sleep tips” are pretty vague or don’t cite a reputable source (‘some say’ or ‘it is thought’ don’t count!), and the app is not great for tracking naps (must sleep for at least 90 mins to count) and the way the days are broken up can cause problems when I fall asleep after midnight.

reviews.title: Fun, Useful, could perform better
reviews.text:
I love the app and use it as my default sleep tracker, but it could use some quality of life adjustments:
1) Make font size adjustable or sync to our device settings. Some of the lettering is tenths of a mm tall on my screen and I can’t even zoom in on it. I stand no chance to read it first thing in the morning.
2) Change it so leveling up Snorlax can not override the sleep screen. But I’ve had multiple times that Snorlax levels up right after I hit confirm to go to sleep and set my phone face down, and it keeps the screen on displaying the level up screen and I’m worried about screen durability when it’s like that all night.
3) Ties in to 2, but really this app needs to be receptive to be able to run in the background with the screen off. My phone is sitting there with the screen technically on and unlocked all night while I sleep, and I’m not super comfortable with that.

I enjoy the app greatly and have used it for a year or two now, but do hope to see the devs find ways to improve on these fronts.

reviews.text: This game was great until you updated the shiny mechanics in the game. I was getting shinys all the time. I barely get them now and I have Pokemon like level 30 and still haven’t seen a shiny of it. When I would get a shiny with them being like level 5. So extremely disappointed with how the game is going now.

reviews.title: After A Month, Meh Over It
reviews.text: First of all, the “glowing” reviews are 100% fake and paid for. Far too detailed, like someone is actually trying to sell you the product itself. While the app is not exactly terrible per say it’s not very accurate at tracking your sleep unless you have an Apple Watch. Tracking on the phone is not that accurate. The gaming aspect of it is also very lacking and kind of forceful. As soon as you wake up you have to do these tasks which sometimes you really don’t want to immediately first thing in the morning. I thought it would be more of and idle game but it actually requires you to be logging in multiple times a day or miss out on “feeding” which then makes your pokemon unhappy and unhelpful. Catching pokemon is the WORST of any pokemon game. You have to give them snacks which itself isn’t that bad, the bad part is how much they cost. A basic poke biscuit is 150 sleep points and the MAX amount you can get in a single day is 100 and that’s only if you get a perfect sleep score. Leveling up and evolving your pokemon is then even harder because it’s not even about hours spent sleeping with a pokemon or just raising its level to a certain point. Nope you gotta keep feeding it level up candy to get it to a certain level and some you have to buy certain stones or items which cost thousands of sleep points. This is honestly the SLOWEST game EVER! Progress is like watching the continents move, yeah it’ll happen after years and years and years of work and dedication which most people will not bother with. If I’m over it after only a month I can’t imagine there are people that will be on it for years and years. You can’t even transfer any pokemon to Pokemon home which would be the ONLY benefit of actually using this app.

reviews.title: Great, but…
reviews.text: Lately, it’s been having an issue where, when I set an alarm for a certain time, it changes whether it’s in the afternoon or the morning. I work late shifts at work. I need my alarm to go off at one PM so I can get to my job at 3 PM, and work until 11 PM. Twice now, it has changed my alarm from 1 PM to 1 AM, causing me to oversleep and have less time to get ready. I’m not sure what’s going on with that, but this NEEDS to get fixed.

reviews.title: Helpful, but lack of music choice
reviews.text: Really have found this app helpful in trying to stick to schedule. However, it could greatly benefit from integrating some music services like Apple, Spotify, etc. as most of the “relaxing” sounds it provides are a little too stimulating to help with sleep.
